A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PhyWorldBench and CAP. All 31 pages of v1 and 35 pages of v2, including appendices, tables and figures, support comparison after matching relocated and renamed content.

before.justification: v1 reports original human evaluations of generated videos, CAP evaluator experiments, prompt comparisons and model-scale analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds numerical CAP scores, static-scene failure analysis and paired prompt experiments.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, binary SA/PC criteria and two-stage context-aware CAP procedure remain unchanged. The evaluator prompts and previously reported fine-tuning experiments are retained; the new failure analyses introduce no method component.

E1.justification: Sections 4.5–4.6 add paired prompt scenarios contrasting abrupt with non-abrupt events and complex with simpler interactions. This modestly extends controlled task conditions within the existing physics domains; the core 1,050-prompt, ten-category benchmark remains unchanged.

E2.justification: The twelve generators, four MLLM evaluator baselines and Cosmos/CogVideo scale comparisons are retained after matching renamed entries. VideoPhy-2 is explicitly excluded from evaluation, while T2VPhysBench enters only the descriptive benchmark comparison.

E3.justification: v2 introduces 20 prompt pairs per abruptness/complexity test and samples 50 failed videos per model for the rationalization analysis. The reported smaller CogVideo variant changes from CogVideo-1.5B to CogVideoX-2B, without establishing a rerun. Existing benchmark procedures remain; the stated 240-video total conflicts with 240 observations per condition in Tables 16–17.

E4.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the supplementary analysis through a systematic study of 600 failures and controlled tests of abrupt visual changes and interaction complexity (Appendices M and Q). v1 discusses and illustrates these problems qualitatively but lacks these quantitative analyses. Existing CAP, prompt and scale ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports generation-seed repetitions, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added success counts and failure percentages do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial quantitative evidence in Tables 7, 13 and 16–17: generator-specific CAP scores, rationalization rates and paired-test outcomes. Overall success is 22.1% versus 42.1% for abrupt/non-abrupt prompts and 11.7% versus 18.3% for complex/simpler prompts. Existing main results and rankings remain unchanged. Two Step-Video-T2V Both values change from 0.25107 to 0.257 for C8 and 0.31466 to 0.316 for C9 (v1 Table 8; v2 Table 9), which is not equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: The binary SA/PC definitions remain unchanged. Neither version introduces formal theorems, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: a comprehensive physics benchmark including anti-physics, CAP evaluation, twelve-model assessment and physics-aware prompting guidance.

C2.justification: Appendix M extends the existing rationalization explanation by arguing that stronger generators increasingly suppress motion after achieving visual and semantic coherence, whereas weaker models fail through geometry or object errors. The previously stated coverage limitations, evaluator aesthetic bias and overconfidence remain.

D1.justification: Table 14 newly discloses video durations: two seconds for Open-Sora, eight for Step-Video-T2V and five for the others; this does not establish changed generation settings. v2 also adds an LLM-usage statement, removes the project-website pointer and abbreviates release details while retaining dataset and code access links.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to VideoPhy-2, WISA, NewtonGen and VideoREPA, expands the main-text discussion of Morpheus, and includes T2VPhysBench in Table 1. Appendix D adds reasons for excluding VideoPhy-2's evaluator. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized rewrites in Sections 4.5–4.7, updated CogVideo naming and affiliations, new administrative statements and appendix headings, and removal of the duplicated main-text Impact Statement while retaining its appendix counterpart.

P2.justification: v2 adopts an ICLR single-column main-text layout and extensively resizes and relocates displays. It adds Tables 7, 13, 14, 16 and 17 and expands Table 1. The existing qualitative examples remain, with higher-resolution imagery in Figure 16.

improvement.justification: The paired controls and systematic failure annotations provide quantitative support for previously anecdotal explanations, while generator-specific CAP scores and disclosed clip lengths improve transparency. These are useful gains around the unchanged core benchmark and evaluator. Their strength is limited by incomplete experimental accounting, particularly the conflict between 240 videos total in Section 4.5 and 240 per condition in the accompanying table.
